solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put in symbols, made fishy?

definitions.meaning: set down systematically as a code or formal system
a playful reading: turned into cod, the fish

explanation.surface: Someone encoded a text and in doing so made it look suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split the word as COD-IFIED and it means turned into a cod.
explanation.definitionFit: To codify is to arrange rules or text into a system of written signs or codes.

clue.text: Bird clocked nuts

definitions.meaning: the bird that pops out of a clock

explanation.surface: A bird spotted some nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clocked' looks like noticed, but it points to the cuckoo clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuckoo is the bird of the cuckoo clock, and cuckoo is also slang for crazy.

clue.text: Ready when derailed to change ticket

indicators.note: a derailed train is thrown off its tracks, so the letters of ready are thrown out of order

parts.note: to turn is to change, as milk turns

explanation.surface: A train is set to switch tickets after it came off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A day return is a British rail ticket to travel out and back on the same day.

clue.text: Round Isle of Man I tripped — in time?

indicators.note: the letters stumble and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller stumbles all round the Isle of Man, wondering whether they will be in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripped' looks like travelled, but signals the anagram. The definition plays on time as the fourth dimension.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-time has three spatial dimensions plus time, so existing in time means having four dimensions.

clue.text: Merlot regularly passed around, it is not for everyone!

indicators.note: the picked letters are passed around the words it is, enclosing them
regularly picks every other letter of the wine name

explanation.surface: A bottle of Merlot is passed round, but it is not for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed around' reads as sharing the wine, but it signals one piece enclosing another.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitist describes something aimed at a select few rather than the whole population.

clue.text: Begging on the throne?

definitions.meaning: reigning, in the role of a monarch, read as two words

explanation.surface: A pauper pleads while seated on the royal seat, or on the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into AS KING: in the capacity of a monarch, i.e. sitting on the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for something is requesting it, which is what a beggar does.

clue.text: Safe and natural cracks under capital in Sacramento, this crack potentially unsafe

indicators.note: in a down answer the shuffled letters sit under, so after, the capital
the capital letter of the city name, its first letter
the words crack apart and reform in a new order

explanation.surface: A safe-looking natural landscape cracks near California's capital: a dangerous fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital in Sacramento' looks like the state capital but means its capital letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: The San Andreas Fault is the Californian geological fault line, a crack in the Earth's crust prone to earthquakes.

clue.text: As Sanskrit and Urdu in mind, I concentrated

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A student focuses hard on Sanskrit and Urdu.
explanation.definitionFit: Indic is the branch of Indo-European languages from the Indian subcontinent, including Sanskrit and Urdu.

clue.text: Cause adopted by cadet, a renegade going the other way

indicators.note: going the other way says the hidden letters are read backwards
a thing adopted by these words is taken into them, so it lies inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cause is taken up by a rebellious young officer heading in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Cause adopted' as the definition, but 'adopted by' is the signal that the letters lie inside 'cadet, a renegade'; the definition is just 'Cause', a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate something is to cause it or bring it into being.

clue.text: Milk in baby feeder for Victoria and Albert, perhaps?

indicators.note: the exploit word goes inside the feeder word

parts.note: a mum feeds her baby
to milk a situation is to use or exploit it

explanation.surface: A royal couple feed their baby milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria and Albert' looks like the royal couple, but it is the V&A, a London museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria and Albert, the V&A, is a famous London museum of art and design.

clue.text: Large rodent, timid baby dropping tail

parts.note: coy means shy or timid

indicators.note: losing its tail tells us to remove the final letter of the baby word

parts.note: a pup is a baby animal such as a young dog or seal

explanation.surface: A big rodent, shy as a youngster, has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu, or nutria, is a big South American water rodent, larger than a rat.

clue.text: Poop deck only starts flooding in for old monster

indicators.note: the poop and the starts pour into the word in, filling it from the middle

parts.note: guano is bird or bat droppings, i.e. poop

indicators.note: the starts of the words deck and only, their first letters

explanation.surface: Waves pour over a ship's raised rear deck, seemingly only at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poop deck' looks like part of a ship, but Poop means bird droppings and deck only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur, a monster from prehistory.

clue.text: Intense state of activity in terms of cricket?

definitions.meaning: a state of frantic effort, as when an engine runs flat out
spoken as cricket words: an over (six balls) and a drive (a forward attacking shot)

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator describes a frenzied burst of play.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a set of six balls and a DRIVE is a batting stroke; the two terms side by side give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Going into overdrive means working at a heightened, frantic level of activity.

clue.text: Conservative kept in check after U-turn, less despicable

indicators.note: the abbreviation is held inside the turned word
after a U-turn the restraining word reads backwards

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A Tory, kept under control after a policy reversal, seems less awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after U-turn' turns REIN into NIER; 'kept in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nicer is more pleasant, the opposite of more despicable.

clue.text: Top calculation a little bit short

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetical calculation

indicators.note: short means the little-bit word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: a mite is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A top-level sum comes up just a fraction short.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the highest point or peak of a mountain.

clue.text: Ideal partner the missus left, it's inferred?

definitions.meaning: if Mrs is on the left, the husband, Mr, must be on the right

explanation.surface: A wife has walked out, so presumably her husband was the perfect match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like departed, but it is a position: with the wife on the left, Mr stands on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the idiom for the perfect man a person hopes to marry.

clue.text: Blow a gasket while following West Indian round block

indicators.note: the while word follows the rest
the Indian word goes round the block word

parts.note: a Goan comes from Goa, a state on the west coast of India
to ban is to block
as can mean while

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper while chasing a Caribbean man round the block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' suggests the Caribbean, but means a person from western India: GOAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Go bananas and blow a gasket are both idioms for losing one's temper.

clue.text: On counter, room key

indicators.note: in a down answer one word on another sits above it, so the room word comes first

parts.note: room means space
a bar is a counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: The room key has been left on the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The space bar is the long key on a keyboard that types a gap.

clue.text: Article confiscated by coppers, as punishment

indicators.note: the article is taken and held by the coppers, so it goes inside

parts.note: coppers are low-value coins, pennies or pence
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Police seize an item as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but here it means copper coins: PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A penance is a self-imposed punishment done to atone for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Dictation of two letters, superfluity

indicators.note: dictating means saying the letters out loud to be written down

parts.note: the letters X and S, which together also mark extra-small

explanation.surface: Taking down a dictation of two letters seems too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess is a surplus, more than is needed.

clue.text: Nipping sideways possibly, cross

definitions.meaning: like a crab, pinching with claws and scuttling sideways

explanation.surface: A grumpy creature scuttles sideways and pinches.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means irritable, and literally means behaving like a crab with its pincers and sideways gait.

clue.text: Bit of butter in range, cut for bread

indicators.note: the butter goes inside the cut range
cut means the range word loses its end

parts.note: a chain is a range, as of mountains
a pat is a small piece of butter

explanation.surface: A piece of butter on the cooking range is spread on cut bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like the stove, but it is a mountain CHAIN, cut to CHAI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread.

clue.text: Care to attack

definitions.meaning: custody or responsibility, as a child in one's keeping
to rush forward against an enemy

explanation.definitionFit: A charge is someone in your care, and to charge is to rush at an enemy.

clue.text: Isle in better state

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: An island seems to be in a better condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better state' reads as an improved condition, but it is CAP (outdo) plus a US state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, Italy.

clue.text: Bits seen as thong pulled up

indicators.note: in a down answer pulling up reads the strap word from the bottom

parts.note: a thong is a leather strap

explanation.surface: Private bits are visible when the thong is pulled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts are pieces or bits of a whole.

clue.text: Slowly move beyond something worthless in flier

indicators.note: the slow-move word comes beyond, that is after, the worthless one

parts.note: chaff is husks, so anything worthless
to inch is to move slowly

explanation.surface: Something creeps along past worthless rubbish in an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaffinch is a common European finch, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Cold water as beer, gin rum!

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the drinks are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: A drinker lists cold refreshments: beer, gin, rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like a third drink but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bering Sea is a freezing northern part of the Pacific between Alaska and Siberia.

clue.text: Au naturel on camera, scrawnier backsides bony?

indicators.note: the backsides of the words are their back ends, their final letters

explanation.surface: Nude on camera, thinner bottoms look bony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsides' fits the nude scene but takes the last letter of each of five words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnar relates to the ulna, a forearm bone, so it is a bone-related adjective.

clue.text: Unsuccessful flankers tackled by prop, score

indicators.note: the flankers are grabbed and held inside the prop word

parts.note: a rest is a support or prop

indicators.note: the flankers of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Rugby: failing wing forwards are stopped by a prop and the score changes.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, flankers and props are forward positions; here they are just letter positions and a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the final score of a match.

clue.text: Test said to bring about a feeling of repugnance

indicators.note: to bring about is to turn around, so the test-said letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A test is reported to cause disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is dislike or aversion, a sense of revulsion.
